title: Audit Planning, Strategy and Execution
outcomes: Plan the audit with an overall strategy and audit plan.
Design and use audit programmes during execution.
Use the work of other auditors, internal auditors and experts.

meta.exam_tip: When others' work is involved, identify the right SA first — 600, 610, 620 or 500.

concepts.title: Commencing the audit, strategy and plan (SA 300)
body: Planning (SA 300) develops an overall audit strategy (scope, timing, direction, reporting objectives, resources) and an audit plan (nature, timing and extent of risk assessment procedures, further procedures and other procedures). Planning is continuous and updated as the audit proceeds; extent depends on size, complexity, experience with the entity and changes.
Before starting: agree terms of engagement (SA 210), perform acceptance and continuance procedures, evaluate ethics and independence, and in an initial audit communicate with the predecessor auditor.
Documentation includes the strategy, plan, significant changes and reasons. Direction, supervision and review of the team are planned according to risk.
concepts.analogy: Strategy sets the direction; the plan sets the steps.
concepts.work: A first-year audit needs more planning time than a recurring one.

concepts.title: Audit programme and execution
body: An audit programme lists procedures for each area, aligned to assertions and risks; it guides staff, records work done and supports review. It must be flexible enough to respond to new findings.
Execution covers planning the fieldwork, understanding and evaluating risks and controls (SA 315), testing controls and performing substantive procedures (SA 330), and reporting.
Other considerations during execution include materiality (SA 320), communications, written representations and documentation (SA 230).
concepts.analogy: Programme the work, then execute it to the risks.
concepts.work: A receivables programme includes confirmations, ageing review and cut-off tests.

concepts.title: Using the work of others: SA 600, SA 610 and SA 620
body: SA 600 (using the work of another auditor): the principal auditor is responsible for the opinion; considers the other auditor's professional competence and independence, communicates requirements, and may review their work; generally no reference to the other auditor is made unless law or practice permits, in which case responsibility is not divided.

SA 610 (internal auditors): evaluate objectivity, competence and systematic approach; decide the extent of use based on risk and judgement involved; perform audit procedures on work used. Internal auditors may provide direct assistance under the external auditor's direction, supervision and review unless law or regulation prohibits it; they cannot be used for work involving significant judgement, higher assessed risks or areas they were involved in.
SA 620 (auditor's expert): evaluate competence, capabilities and objectivity; agree scope and objectives in writing; evaluate adequacy of findings. No reference to the expert in an unmodified report.
concepts.analogy: Use others' work, but never hand over responsibility.
concepts.work: An auditor uses an actuary for gratuity but still owns the conclusion.

concepts.title: Accounting estimates (SA 540)
body: Accounting estimates (provisions, fair values, impairment, ECL, useful lives) involve estimation uncertainty, complexity and subjectivity. SA 540 (Revised) requires understanding how management makes estimates and assessing inherent risk factors.

Responses: test how management made the estimate (methods, data, assumptions), develop an auditor's point estimate or range, or use events up to the report date. Evaluate management bias indicators and adequacy of disclosures about uncertainty.
Retrospective review of prior-period estimates helps identify bias and the effectiveness of management's process.
concepts.analogy: Estimates are judgements — audit the method, data and assumptions.
concepts.work: Comparing last year's warranty provision with actual claims tests estimation quality.

concepts.title: Evaluating misstatements (SA 450)
body: SA 450 requires accumulating misstatements other than clearly trivial ones. Types: factual (no doubt), judgemental (differences in estimates or policies) and projected (extrapolated from samples).
Misstatements are communicated to management for correction; if uncorrected, the auditor considers their size and nature individually and in aggregate, qualitative factors, and effect on materiality.

Uncorrected misstatements are communicated to TCWG, a written representation obtained that management believes their effect is immaterial, and documentation kept. If material, the opinion is modified.
concepts.analogy: Add up what is wrong, ask for correction, and judge what remains.
concepts.work: Uncorrected errors of ₹45 lakh against ₹50 lakh materiality leave little headroom.

illustrations.title: Accumulating misstatements
illustrations.q: Overall materiality for Vega Ltd. is ₹50 lakh; the auditor treats amounts below 5% of materiality as clearly trivial. Uncorrected misstatements: a factual cut-off error of ₹18 lakh, a judgemental difference on a provision of ₹12 lakh, and a projected misstatement from sampling of ₹15 lakh. Management refuses to correct them. Evaluate under SA 450.

illustrations.title: Can we use their work?
illustrations.q: The auditor of Nova Ltd. wants to (a) use the internal audit team's inventory counts; (b) ask internal auditors to directly assist in testing payables; (c) rely on a property valuer appointed by management; (d) use another firm's audit of a branch. Which SA applies and what must be evaluated?

jobs.title: Planning a group audit kick-off
jobs.situation: A new manufacturing client with two branches audited by other firms.
steps: Agree engagement terms and communicate with predecessor.
Decide use of internal audit and experts.
jobs.takeaway: Good planning decides how much reliance on others is safe.

mistakes: Using direct assistance for significant judgements.

summary: Audit programme tied to risks and assertions.
remember: Direct assistance is allowed only if law does not prohibit it, and never for significant judgements.

viva.q: Distinguish the overall audit strategy and the audit plan.
viva.model: The strategy sets scope, timing and direction; the plan details the nature, timing and extent of procedures.

viva.q: What does the auditor evaluate before using internal audit work?
viva.model: The internal audit function's objectivity, competence and systematic and disciplined approach.

viva.q: What are the three types of misstatement under SA 450?
How can an auditor respond to risks in estimates?
viva.model: Test management's process, develop an independent point estimate or range, or use events up to the report date.

viva.q: Does using an expert reduce the auditor's responsibility?
viva.model: It leaves the auditor solely responsible for the opinion.

cases.title: Lotus Hotels Ltd.
cases.case: Lotus Hotels has properties revalued by an external valuer appointed by management. The statutory auditor engages its own IT specialist. A branch in Goa is audited by another firm. Internal auditors offer to test room revenue directly under the statutory auditor's supervision.

mcqs.q: The valuer appointed by Lotus is:
mcqs.explain: Evaluate under SA 500. In practice: assess objectivity.
mcqs.topic: Using the work of others: SA 600, SA 610 and SA 620

mcqs.q: The IT specialist engaged by the auditor is governed by:
mcqs.explain: Auditor's expert. In practice: written agreement.
mcqs.topic: Using the work of others: SA 600, SA 610 and SA 620

mcqs.q: The offer of direct assistance on room revenue testing can be accepted only if:
options: Not prohibited by law, objectivity and competence are adequate, and the work is supervised and reviewed
mcqs.explain: SA 610 conditions. In practice: avoid significant judgement areas.
mcqs.topic: Using the work of others: SA 600, SA 610 and SA 620

mcqs.q: Work of the Goa branch auditor is considered under:
mcqs.explain: Using work of another auditor. In practice: Companies Act section 143(8).
mcqs.topic: Using the work of others: SA 600, SA 610 and SA 620
